summary: The minimum feasible operation count, when one exists under the integer bounds, is found among the fixed candidates 1 through 60, so varying the numeric inputs cannot create an honest asymptotic runtime-scaling experiment.

workload_bound.source_constraint: Each operation chooses an exponent i in [0, 60], and the bounded-input feasibility argument requires testing only k = 1 through 60.

replacement_checks.evidence: Each of the 60 candidates performs fixed-width subtraction, multiplication, comparison, and population-count work; every adjusted value is bounded by 61,000,000,000 and therefore has at most 36 relevant bits.

Authored cases cover zero, positive, and negative num2; minimum and billion-scale inputs; impossible nonpositive adjusted remainders; one-operation results; and feasible answers requiring many candidates.
